s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive subcutaneous node in the axilla with skin infiltration and possible hormonal influence
salient_findings: Slowly growing subcutaneous node in the right axilla
Progressive infiltration of the overlying skin
Erythematous plaque in the right axilla measuring 5 × 3 cm
Dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement
Tumor cells with 'Indian file pattern' and positive for specific antibodies
key_facts: Woman in her 60s
Subcutaneous node in the right axilla first noticed 10 years ago
Progressive infiltration of the overlying skin over the past year
Swelling in the right axilla during pregnancy over 20 years ago
Mild episodic pain in the right axilla during menstrual cycles
Solitary, indolent, erythematous plaque in the right axilla measuring 5 × 3 cm
Dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement
Tumor cells diffusely dispersed between collagen bundles and lined up in an 'Indian file pattern'
Tumor cells have basophilic nuclei and scant cytoplasm
Positive for pancytokeratin (AE1/AE3), cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies
Negative for synaptophysin, chromogranin, and S100-stainings
Multiple GATA3-positive and estrogen receptor–positive apocrine glands in close association to diffuse tumor cell infiltration
1 of the sentinel lymph nodes showed isolated cytokeratin8/18–positive tumor cells and MNF116-positive tumor cells
No evidence of primary or secondary tumors on chest, abdominal, and pelvic CT scans, cranial and breast MRI, mammography, and breast sonography

shortlist.label: Hidradenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches histopathology and immunohistochemistry findings, including positive staining for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3

shortlist.label: Apocrine gland carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Supported by the presence of multiple GATA3-positive and estrogen receptor–positive apocrine glands in close association to diffuse tumor cell infiltration

shortlist.label: Syringomatous apocrine carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with the 'Indian file pattern' of tumor cells and the expression of apocrine markers

shortlist.label: Tubular apocrine adenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Fits with the clinical presentation of a slowly growing subcutaneous node and the histological features of tubular structures

shortlist.label: Mammary analogue secretory carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Considered due to the positive staining for GATA3 and estrogen receptor, and the presence of a subcutaneous node with skin infiltration
